opening_actions: Places a weighted torso block onto a slender scaled human leg armature.
Observes the thin leg frame splinter and collapse under the proportional load.
Steps to an adjacent stone display pedestal holding a heavy leather-bound volume.

entry_bridge.a_end: The scholar rests his palm on an embossed topic book resting on a stone display pedestal.
entry_bridge.b_start: Top-down view of the closed book bound in rough hide-textured leather on the pedestal.
entry_bridge.reveal: The book falls open to an illustrated structural comparison of slender angled human legs beside massive elephant pillar legs.
entry_bridge.world_entry: A colossal four-ton human figure collapses onto its knees as slender leg bones buckle under the body mass.

opening_activity: Testing how scaling weight without widening bone thickness breaks upright support.
opening_location: Outdoor comparative biomechanics pavilion beside life-size animal leg casts.
opening_environment: An open-air stone pavilion lined with mammalian skeletal casts and mechanical load test rigs under clear morning daylight.
topic_visual_link: A physical load test directly demonstrates how human leg proportions fail catastrophically when forced to support elephant-scale weight.
opening_visual_proof: A slender wooden leg armature scaled to human proportions snaps cleanly under a simulated four-ton torso block.
curiosity_trigger: The sudden crack of the slender model leg giving way beneath the weighted block.
trigger_object: A splintering model leg armature crushed under a weighted torso block.
reaction: A quiet blink of surprise followed by a gentle fingertip tap on the fractured timber.
entry_retrieval: Steps over to a stone display pedestal and unlatches the clasp of a thick discovered volume.
world_style_hint: Anatomically grounded biomechanics world featuring massive scale contrasts, volumetric cross-sections, and dynamic stress vectors.
reason: Direct mechanical load failure cleanly grounds the square-cube law in physical evidence before expanding the inquiry to full elephant scale.
